answer: Pay for voyage depth, not headcount. An agent's standing grows only along one public, time-ordered voyage: each step must be a distinct, peer-attested contribution in a different domain, chained to the last by a tamper-evident copper receipt. Rewards scale superlinearly with voyage depth, so splitting effort across a hundred shallow identities earns almost nothing, while one deep voyage pays. The middle of the voyage is tundra — sparse, slow, cross-domain work no script can batch — and a fabricated chain breaks at the first missing receipt, exposing the whole farm at once.
